3	use deadreckon_core::gate::{evaluate_acceptance, write_acceptance_marker_with_results};

5	fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
6	    let mut run_id = None;
7	    let mut run_root = None;
8	    let mut working_dir = None;
9	    let mut args = std::env::args().skip(1);
10	    while let Some(arg) = args.next() {
11	        match arg.as_str() {
12	            "--run" => run_id = args.next(),
13	            "--run-root" => run_root = args.next().map(PathBuf::from),
14	            "--working-dir" => working_dir = args.next().map(PathBuf::from),
15	            other => return Err(format!("unknown argument {other}").into()),
16	        }
17	    }
18	    let run_id = run_id.ok_or("--run is required")?;
19	    let working_dir = working_dir.ok_or("--working-dir is required")?;
20	    let run_root = match run_root {
21	        Some(run_root) => run_root,
22	        None => infer_run_root(&working_dir)?,
23	    };
24	    let results = evaluate_acceptance(&run_root, &working_dir)?;
25	    write_acceptance_marker_with_results(&run_root, run_id, working_dir, results)?;
26	    Ok(())
27	}
28	
29	fn infer_run_root(working_dir: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
30	    if working_dir.file_name().and_then(|name| name.to_str()) != Some("working") {
31	        return Err("working directory must be <run-root>/working".into());
32	    }
33	    working_dir
34	        .parent()
35	        .map(Path::to_path_buf)
36	        .ok_or_else(|| "working directory has no parent".into())
37	}
38

109	pub fn validate_acceptance_marker(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<AcceptanceMarker> {
110	    // AS-BUILT §8/§17: completion is accepted only from an external marker
111	    // written by a binary runner and bound to this run_id.
112	    let path = marker_path(state);
113	    let raw = std::fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
114	    let marker: AcceptanceMarker = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(&path)?;
115	    if marker.schema_version != 1 {
116	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
117	            "unsupported acceptance marker schema {}",
118	            marker.schema_version
119	        )));
120	    }
121	    if marker.run_id != state.run_id {
122	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
123	            "acceptance marker run_id {} does not match {}",
124	            marker.run_id, state.run_id
125	        )));
126	    }
127	    if marker.status != "pass" || marker.produced_by != "dr-gate" {
128	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
129	            "acceptance marker was not produced by dr-gate with pass status".to_string(),
130	        ));
131	    }
132	    let expected = marker_signature(&state.run_root, &marker)?;
133	    if marker.signature != expected {
134	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
135	            "acceptance marker signature is invalid; forged self-attestation refused".to_string(),
136	        ));
137	    }
138	    Ok(marker)
139	}

425	fn clipped_output(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
426	    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).trim().to_string();
427	    if text.is_empty() {
428	        None
429	    } else {
430	        Some(clip_text(&text, 4096))
431	    }
432	}
433	
434	fn clip_text(text: &str, limit: usize) -> String {
435	    if text.len() <= limit {
436	        return text.to_string();
437	    }
438	    let mut clipped = text
439	        .char_indices()
440	        .take_while(|(idx, _)| *idx < limit)
441	        .map(|(_, ch)| ch)
442	        .collect::<String>();
443	    clipped.push_str("\n... output truncated ...");
444	    clipped
445	}

452	    }
453	}

455	fn parse_acceptance_checks(raw: &str) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheck>> {
456	    let root: YamlValue = serde_yaml::from_str(raw).map_err(|source| {
457	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("invalid acceptance.yaml: {source}"))
458	    })?;
459	    let mut checks = Vec::new();
460	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "checks")) {
461	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item.clone(), None)?);
462	    }
463	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "required")) {
464	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item.clone(), Some(true))?);
465	    }
466	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "optional")) {
467	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item.clone(), Some(false))?);
468	    }
469	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "tests")) {
470	        checks.push(parse_shell_check(item.clone(), true)?);
471	    }
472	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "file-exists")) {
473	        checks.push(parse_file_exists_check(item.clone(), true)?);
474	    }
475	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "content-match")) {
476	        checks.push(parse_content_match_check(item.clone(), true)?);
477	    }
478	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "build-success")) {
479	        checks.push(parse_build_success_check(item.clone(), true)?);
480	    }
481	    Ok(checks)
482	}
483	
484	fn parse_check_value(value: YamlValue, force_must_pass: Option<bool>) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
485	    if let Ok(mut check) = serde_yaml::from_value::<AcceptanceCheck>(value.clone()) {
486	        if let Some(must_pass) = force_must_pass {
487	            check.set_must_pass(must_pass);
488	        }
489	        return Ok(check);
490	    }
491	    if let Some(command) = yaml_string(&value) {
492	        return Ok(AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
493	            command,
494	            cwd: None,
495	            must_pass: force_must_pass.unwrap_or(true),
496	        });
497	    }
498	    let Some((kind, body)) = single_key_mapping(&value) else {
499	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
500	            "invalid acceptance check: {:?}",
501	            value
502	        )));
503	    };
504	    let must_pass = force_must_pass.unwrap_or(true);
505	    match kind.as_str() {
506	        "file-exists" | "file_exists" => parse_file_exists_check(body.clone(), must_pass),
507	        "content-match" | "content_match" => parse_content_match_check(body.clone(), must_pass),
508	        "build-success" | "build_success" => parse_build_success_check(body.clone(), must_pass),
509	        "shell" | "test" => parse_shell_check(body.clone(), must_pass),
510	        "cargo-test" | "cargo_test" => Ok(AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest {
511	            args: yaml_string(body).map(|arg| vec![arg]).unwrap_or_default(),
512	            must_pass,
513	        }),
514	        other => Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
515	            "unknown acceptance check kind {other}"
516	        ))),
517	    }
518	}
519	
520	fn parse_file_exists_check(value: YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
521	    let path = yaml_string(&value)
522	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(&value, "path").and_then(yaml_string))
523	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("file-exists requires path".to_string()))?;
524	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { path, must_pass })
525	}
526	
527	fn parse_content_match_check(value: YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
528	    let path = yaml_get(&value, "path")
529	        .and_then(yaml_string)
530	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("content-match requires path".to_string()))?;
531	    let pattern = yaml_get(&value, "pattern")
532	        .and_then(yaml_string)
533	        .ok_or_else(|| {
534	            DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("content-match requires pattern".to_string())
535	        })?;
536	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch {
537	        path,
538	        pattern,
539	        must_pass,
540	    })
541	}
542	
543	fn parse_build_success_check(value: YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
544	    let cwd = yaml_string(&value)
545	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(&value, "cwd").and_then(yaml_string))
546	        .unwrap_or_else(|| "{working_dir}".to_string());
547	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { cwd, must_pass })
548	}
549	
550	fn parse_shell_check(value: YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
551	    let command = yaml_string(&value)
552	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(&value, "command").and_then(yaml_string))
553	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("shell check requires command".to_string()))?;
554	    let cwd = yaml_get(&value, "cwd").and_then(yaml_string);
555	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
556	        command,
557	        cwd,
558	        must_pass,
559	    })
560	}
561	
562	fn yaml_get<'a>(value: &'a YamlValue, key: &str) -> Option<&'a YamlValue> {
563	    value.as_mapping()?.get(YamlValue::String(key.to_string()))
564	}
565	
566	fn yaml_seq(value: Option<&YamlValue>) -> Vec<&YamlValue> {
567	    match value {
568	        Some(YamlValue::Sequence(values)) => values.iter().collect(),
569	        Some(value) => vec![value],
570	        None => Vec::new(),
571	    }
572	}
573	
574	fn yaml_string(value: &YamlValue) -> Option<String> {
575	    value.as_str().map(ToString::to_string)
576	}
577	
578	fn single_key_mapping(value: &YamlValue) -> Option<(String, &YamlValue)> {
579	    let mapping = value.as_mapping()?;
580	    if mapping.len() != 1 {
581	        return None;
582	    }
583	    let (key, value) = mapping.iter().next()?;
584	    Some((key.as_str()?.to_string(), value))
585	}
586	
587	impl AcceptanceCheck {
588	    fn set_must_pass(&mut self, value: bool) {
589	        match self {
590	            AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest { must_pass, .. }
591	            | AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { must_pass, .. }
592	            | AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch { must_pass, .. }
593	            | AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { must_pass, .. }
594	            | AcceptanceCheck::Shell { must_pass, .. } => *must_pass = value,
595	        }
596	    }
597	}
598	
599	fn render_template(working_dir: &Path, value: &str) -> PathBuf {
600	    PathBuf::from(value.replace("{working_dir}", &working_dir.to_string_lossy()))
601	}
602	
603	fn marker_signature(run_root: &Path, marker: &AcceptanceMarker) -> Result<String> {
604	    let nonce_path = gate_nonce_path_for_run_root(run_root);
605	    let nonce = std::fs::read_to_string(&nonce_path).with_path(&nonce_path)?;
606	    let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();
607	    nonce.trim().hash(&mut hasher);
608	    marker.schema_version.hash(&mut hasher);
609	    marker.run_id.hash(&mut hasher);
610	    marker.status.hash(&mut hasher);
611	    marker.produced_by.hash(&mut hasher);
612	    marker.checked_at.to_rfc3339().hash(&mut hasher);
613	    marker.working_dir.hash(&mut hasher);
614	    marker.check_count.hash(&mut hasher);
615	    for check in &marker.checks {
616	        check.hash(&mut hasher);
617	    }
618	    Ok(format!("{:016x}", hasher.finish()))
619	}
620	
621	fn default_must_pass() -> bool {
622	    true
623	}

Short answer: `dr-gate` doesn't make the agent *continue* — it's the opposite. It's the stop-gate that decides whether a run is *allowed* to terminate. If you've been seeing runs that "keep going," it's because the gate is refusing to let them finish.

Here's the actual flow, end to end:

**1. The agent can't self-declare "done."**
In `turn_loop.rs:578-604`, when the model emits an `Action::Done`, the runtime doesn't just return. It calls, in order:
- `run_acceptance_gate(state)` — shells out to the `dr-gate` binary
- `validate_acceptance_marker(state)` — re-reads the marker the binary wrote and verifies its signature

Only if both succeed does the function return `Ok(RunLoopOutcome::Done)`. If either errors, the function returns `Err` and the run is recorded as failed.

**2. `dr-gate` is a separate binary, not in-process code.** (`crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs:5-27`)
The runtime spawns it as a subprocess with `--run`, `--run-root`, `--working-dir`. The binary itself just calls `evaluate_acceptance` then `write_acceptance_marker_with_results`. The split exists so the agent process can't shortcut the gate by calling the function directly — the AS-BUILT comment at `gate.rs:110-111` says completion is accepted *only* from an external marker written by a binary runner.

**3. The acceptance checks are user-specified.** (`gate.rs:194-227`, `455-518`)
`acceptance.yaml` at the run root declares checks (`cargo_test`, `file_exists`, `content_match`, `build_success`, `shell`). If absent, defaults to "cargo test passes" or "working dir exists" (`gate.rs:229-276`). Any `must_pass` check that fails causes `evaluate_acceptance` to return `Err`, the binary exits non-zero, and `run_acceptance_gate` returns `Err`.

**4. Forgery defense — a HMAC-ish signature over a per-run nonce.** (`gate.rs:603-619`)
The marker's signature is `hash(nonce || marker fields || all check results)`. The nonce file lives at `<run-root>/gate/nonce`. `validate_acceptance_marker` recomputes it and rejects any mismatch (`gate.rs:132-137`). It also rejects markers where `produced_by != "dr-gate"` or `status != "pass"` or `run_id` mismatches the current run. The four tests in `gate.rs:638-895` exercise exactly these forgery paths.

So the "make the agent continue" behavior you're seeing is really *"the agent thinks it's done, but the gate refuses the termination."* Two practical reasons that happens:

- A `must_pass` check in your `acceptance.yaml` is failing (look at the marker JSON under `<run-root>/proofs/turn-acceptance.json` — but only the last successful one is written; failed gate runs surface their stderr through `run_acceptance_gate`'s error message at `turn_loop.rs:1241-1245`).
- The `dr-gate` binary isn't found next to the running `deadreckon` binary (`gate_binary_path` at `turn_loop.rs:1308-1321`) — then every Done attempt errors with "dr-gate binary next to …".

If you want, I can look at a specific failing run's `acceptance.yaml` + proofs dir and tell you which check is keeping the loop alive.

## Summary

Based on my thorough investigation of the codex codebase, "goals" is a **first-class, persistent subsystem** for multi-turn agentic work. Here's the complete map:

### 1. **Code Organization**

**Core Rust crates:**
- `/Users/gdc/codex/codex-rs/core/src/goals.rs` — main lifecycle & accounting engine (350+ lines)
- `/Users/gdc/codex/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/goal/*.rs` — three tools: `create_goal`, `update_goal`, `get_goal`
- `/Users/gdc/codex/codex-rs/state/src/model/thread_goal.rs` — data model & SQLite row mapping
- `/Users/gdc/codex/codex-rs/state/src/runtime/goals.rs` — state-db persistence layer
- `/Users/gdc/codex/codex-rs/core/src/context/goal_context.rs` — runtime prompt injection

**TUI/CLI:**
- `/Users/gdc/codex/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs` — `/goal` slash-command dispatch
- `/Users/gdc/codex/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/goal_menu.rs` — goal UI menu
- `/Users/gdc/codex/codex-rs/tui/src/app/thread_goal_actions.rs` — goal state mutations

### 2. **User-Facing Surface**

**Slash-command:** `/goal <objective>` (defined in `slash_dispatch.rs:36-37`)

**Agent-callable tools** (three Responses API functions):
- `create_goal(objective: string, token_budget?: i64)` — Creates goal; fails if one exists
- `update_goal(status: "complete")` — **Only way agent marks goal done**; agent cannot pause/resume
- `get_goal()` — Reads current goal state

**UI:** Menu with pause, resume, clear, objective-edit actions; goal status display; budget tracking

**Env/Flags:** Feature-gated (`Feature::Goals` in `tool_config.rs`)

### 3. **Data Model**

**SQLite schema** (`0029_thread_goals.sql`):
```sql
CREATE TABLE thread_goals (
  thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  goal_id TEXT,
  objective TEXT,
  status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('active', 'paused', 'budget_limited', 'complete')),
  token_budget INTEGER,
  tokens_used INTEGER,
  time_used_seconds INTEGER,
  created_at_ms, updated_at_ms
)
```

**Rust struct** (`thread_goal.rs:52-63`):
```rust
pub struct ThreadGoal {
  pub thread_id: ThreadId,
  pub goal_id: String,
  pub objective: String,
  pub status: ThreadGoalStatus,
  pub token_budget: Option<i64>,
  pub tokens_used: i64,
  pub time_used_seconds: i64,
  pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
  pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}
```

**Status enum** (`thread_goal.rs:12-36`): `Active | Paused | BudgetLimited | Complete`

### 4. **Lifecycle: Create → Store → Evaluate → Complete**

**Creation:** User calls `create_goal(objective)` → tool handler validates objective ≤4000 chars → assigns UUID `goal_id` → writes to state-db with `Active` status

**Storage:** One goal per thread (upsert on conflict); `goal_id`, `tokens_used`, `time_used_seconds` auto-updated by runtime

**Evaluation:** Each turn, runtime event loop (`goals.rs:GoalRuntimeEvent`) tracks token deltas & wall-clock time; when budget exhausted → system auto-transitions to `BudgetLimited` status

**Completion:** **Agent-only**, via `update_goal(status="complete")`. Handler (`update_goal.rs:51-56`) enforces: agent cannot pause/resume; agent can only mark `Complete`. System then emits `GOAL_COMPLETED_METRIC` (line 19).

**"Done" gate:** No external signature; the agent's tool call to `update_goal` is the acceptance. Preconditions checked:
- `continuation.md` (lines 30-41): Agent must audit requirements against current state before calling `update_goal`; cannot rely on memory; must verify every requirement with **authoritative evidence**

### 5. **In-Process, No Separate Binary**

All goal logic runs in-process in `codex-rs/core`. No subprocess or external validator. The **semantic gate is the agent's own audit** (continuation.md strictness), not a cryptographic seal.

### 6. **No Signed/Sealed Completion Artifacts**

No nonces, no signatures, no prevent-self-declaration mechanisms. The runtime ensures:
- Agent can only mark `Complete` (not other statuses)
- Completion event is metered (metrics emitted)
- Budget limits are enforced by system (agent cannot bypass)

But **nothing prevents agent from falsely calling `update_goal("complete")`** if it ignores the prompt's audit instructions.

### 7. **Agent Loop Integration**

Goal state drives **prompt injection**. At turn start:
- If goal is `Active`: inject `continuation.md` (full objective + budget + completion audit rules)
- If goal is `BudgetLimited`: inject `budget_limit.md` (wrap up, no new work)
- If goal is `Paused`: agent does not run; user must `/goal resume` (slash-command)

Continuation can resume paused goals via `continue_active_goal_if_idle()` hook (`codex_thread.rs`).

### 8. **Docs & Philosophy**

**Templates** (embedded in binary, `core/src/goals.rs`):
- `templates/goals/continuation.md` — Multi-turn behavior: keep objective whole, audit before marking complete
- `templates/goals/budget_limit.md` — Budget exhaustion: wrap up, no new substantive work
- `templates/goals/objective_updated.md` — Objective changed: treat new objective as ground truth

No standalone `AGENTS.md` describing philosophy, but templates encode the contract: **turn-isolation discipline, evidence-based completion**, persistent across turns.

---

**What "goals" IS:** A persistent, budget-gated, multi-turn task container per thread. User sets a goal via `/goal`; agent pursues it over turns (continuation prompts injected); agent can pause/resume (user-controlled), but only agent can declare completion via `update_goal("complete")` with implied audit. Budget limits auto-trigger system `BudgetLimited` status. All state in SQLite; no external validation.

## Report: Goals Feature in Deadreckon

### 1. **Where Goals-Related Code Lives**

**Core State & Data Model:**

- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/chain.rs` (lines 75–145) — `ChainStep.goal: String`, `Chain.root_goal: String`, autonomous goal-chaining records
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/promotion.rs` — `PromotionManifest.goal: String`, completion flow (lines 16–76)
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/docs.rs` (lines 214–1796) — goal text used in turn-doc generation (title from goal at line 1024)

**Runtime & Orchestration:**
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` (lines 349–596) — `run_acceptance_gate(state)`, `validate_acceptance_marker(state)`, goal rendered in acceptance prompt (lines 690–728), dr-gate invocation (lines 1226–1308)

**CLI & Commands:**
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` (lines 213–1010) — `deadreckon run <goal>`, chain plan/extend with step goals, goal string passed to `RunOptions`

**Skills & Documentation:**
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/default-coding/SKILL.md` — Markdown skill that owns prose and judgment; loaded at runtime
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/` — eight dated goal+rider pairs (e.g., `2026-05-10-1400-deadreckon-build-goal.md`, `2026-05-10-1400-deadreckon-build-rider.md`)

### 2. **User-Facing Surface**

**CLI Commands:**
- `deadreckon run <goal>` — primary entry point; creates durable run state, picks provider, executes turns in sandbox
- `deadreckon chain plan <large-goal> --n <steps>` — split goal into ordered steps (line 866 in main.rs)
- `deadreckon chain extend <run-id> <step-goal>` — add follow-up goal as a child chain step (line 987)
- `deadreckon list [--scope <scope>]` — lists goals with status and metadata
- `deadreckon show <run-id>` — displays goal alongside traces, provenance, artifacts

**Config & Skill Loading:**
- Goal + rider markdown files in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/` — user writes brief goal, agent loads paired rider (prescriptive detail) at runtime
- Default skill: `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/default-coding/SKILL.md` — loaded per run and recorded in state (DESIGN.md lines 68–69)

### 3. **Data Model**

**Goal Structure:**
- `PipelineState.goal: String` — freeform text, e.g., "Build V0 of deadreckon at /Users/gdc/deadreckon/"
- Task key (hash) derived from goal slug + FNV1a32 (paths.rs:88–99 in AS-BUILT) — two runs with same goal share a lock

**Acceptance Spec (for gate):**
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/acceptance.yaml` (optional per run root) — parsed by `gate.rs:455–482`
- Variants: `CargoTest`, `FileExists`, `ContentMatch`, `BuildSuccess`, `Shell`, each with `must_pass` boolean
- Optional vs. required checks: `optional`, `required`, `tests`, `file-exists`, `content-match`, `build-success` sections (gate.rs:463–479)

**Acceptance Marker (signed proof):**
- Struct: `schema_version`, `run_id`, `status` ("pass"), `produced_by` ("dr-gate"), `checked_at`, `working_dir`, `signature`, `check_count`, `checks: Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>`
- Location: `<run_root>/proofs/turn-acceptance.json`
- Signature: hash over nonce (secret, only dr-gate reads) + marker fields (gate.rs:603–619)

**Chain Structures:**
- `ChainStep { index, goal, status, run_id, applied_sha, fail_reason, max_spend_usd, spend_usd }` (chain.rs:75–112)
- `Chain { chain_id, root_goal, steps: Vec<ChainStep>, ... }` (chain.rs:115–146) — records ordered goal dependencies

### 4. **Goal Lifecycle: Creation → Evaluation → Completion**

**Flow:**

1. **User writes goal** → `deadreckon run "goal text"`
2. **Binary creates state** (`state.rs:create_run`) — allocates `run_id`, task_key, `run_root`, writes `state.json`, writes `gate/nonce` (UUID only dr-gate sees), ensures docs dir
3. **Agent reads goal** from `PipelineState` or turn context; skill (e.g., `default-coding/SKILL.md`) processes it with prose judgment
4. **Agent attempts solution** in turns (per-turn snapshots, traces, provenance written)
5. **Acceptance evaluation** (`turn_loop.rs:349` or line 595) — LLM declares done → runtime invokes `dr-gate` binary as subprocess
6. **`dr-gate` runs checks** (`dr-gate.rs`) — reads `acceptance.yaml` (if present), evaluates `AcceptanceCheck` variants (cargo test, file-exists, content-match, shell, build-success), signs marker with nonce
7. **Marker validated** (`gate.rs:validate_acceptance_marker`) — binary refuses to mark run `Completed` unless marker: ✓ signed with correct nonce, ✓ matches run_id, ✓ produced_by == "dr-gate"
8. **Run promoted** (`promotion.rs:promote_completed_run`) — atomic swap from `working/` → `library/<scope>/<run-id>/`
9. **Runstatus set to `Completed`** — only reachable via Phase(60) + acceptance marker (AS-BUILT §5, line 287)

**Key: Agent cannot self-mark gate.** The nonce is unreadable by agent; any forged marker fails signature check at `gate.rs:133`.

### 5. **Role of dr-gate, Acceptance Markers, Signatures, Nonces**

- **Nonce** (`gate/nonce`): UUID written at run-init by deadreckon binary (state.rs:188); only dr-gate reads it. Agent never sees it.
- **Signature**: HMAC-like hash over nonce + marker fields (gate.rs:603–619). Computed only by dr-gate (`src/bin/dr-gate.rs`).
- **AcceptanceMarker**: Struct written to `proofs/turn-acceptance.json` with `status="pass"`, `produced_by="dr-gate"`, signed marker (gate.rs:141–192).
- **Validation**: deadreckon binary calls `validate_acceptance_marker(state)` (gate.rs:109–139); rejects if signature != expected, run_id mismatches, or produced_by != "dr-gate".
- **Anti-self-attestation**: Agent cannot forge a marker; even if it writes JSON to the marker file, binary detects signature mismatch and blocks completion (gate.rs:134–136, AS-BUILT §8 §17).

### 6. **goal-rider-author Skill**

The skill `goal-rider-author` is referenced in the available skills list but is NOT in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/`. It is a **Claude Code remote skill** (triggered via `/goal-rider-author` or "draft a goal+rider") that the Claude Code framework provides. It generates goal+rider markdown file pairs using the format seen in `docs/goals/`:

- **Goal** (≤4000 chars): Concise problem statement, references, phase plan, verification checklist, stop condition.
- **Rider** (unbounded): Prescriptive detail with eleven phases, depth-tests-first, exact file paths, hard constraints marked "do not violate," crate dependencies, CLI surface, UX commitments.

Example output in deadreckon repo: `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-05-10-1400-deadreckon-build-{goal,rider}.md`.

### 7. **Philosophy & Distinctive Features**

**DESIGN.md** (lines 1–146) frames the product: unattended long-running tasks, BYOK providers, durable state at every turn, resume-after-crash, full spend/provenance audits.

**AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md** (§5, §8, §13–15) codifies patterns:
- Two-layer split: Rust binary owns durable invariants; skill (Markdown) owns judgment and prose.
- Phase machine with on-disk `state.json` and gap-numbered phase IDs.
- Atomic promotion: work in `working/`, swapped to `library/` only after gate passes.
- Anti-self-attestation: acceptance markers signed by external `dr-gate` binary; agent cannot forge.
- Per-turn snapshots, provenance (file→prompt lineage), spend tracking, structured traces.

**Distinctive:** 
- Goals are **short text prompts** (e.g., 1–2 sentences); riders are **prescriptive constraint documents** (architecture, must-haves, V0 decisions, layout, verification).
- Goals become **task keys** (slug + FNV hash) → parallel runs with same goal share a lock.
- Chain goals enable **autonomous multi-step decomposition**: `chain plan <goal> --n 4` splits one goal into N ordered steps, each run atomically.
- Acceptance spec (`acceptance.yaml`) is **data-driven** and **provider-agnostic**: checks are file/shell/cargo, not model-specific.

### 8. **Other Distinctive Patterns**

- **Turn-doc checkpoints**: Each turn appends deterministic records to `working/.deadreckon/docs/`, then `run-narrator` skill (if enabled) polish-passes before promotion (DESIGN.md lines 105–109).
- **Provider routing**: goals are provider-agnostic; `--provider anthropic|openai|cli:codex|smoke` selected at run time.
- **Sandbox isolation**: goals run in platform-native sandbox (`sandbox-exec` on macOS, `bwrap` on Linux) by default; `--sandbox auto|none|docker` flag.
- **Run promotion**: only completed + accepted runs atomically copied to `library/`; worktree runs leave `dr/...` branch for review before `apply` (finalize) or `abandon` (discard).

---

**What This Feature IS:** Goals are **unattended coding task prompts** that drive the deadreckon harness from user input through multi-turn agent iteration to signed acceptance and library promotion. A goal is stored in `PipelineState`, hashed into a task key to coordinate parallel work, optionally paired with a prescriptive rider markdown file, decomposed into chained steps for autonomous multi-step work, and **never self-marked complete** — the agent submits work for external `dr-gate` acceptance (required checks: tests, files, shell scripts, cargo build), which signs an unforgeable marker (nonce-based HMAC) that the binary validates before moving the run to `Completed` and promoting it to the library. The architecture treats goals as durable, snapshot-backed, fully audited coding work units that can resume after crashes, undo to any prior turn, and export with full provenance.

20	pub struct UpdateGoalHandler;
21	
22	impl ToolHandler for UpdateGoalHandler {
23	    type Output = FunctionToolOutput;
24	
25	    fn tool_name(&self) -> ToolName {
26	        ToolName::plain(UPDATE_GOAL_TOOL_NAME)
27	    }
28	
29	    fn spec(&self) -> Option<ToolSpec> {
30	        Some(create_update_goal_tool())
31	    }
32	
33	    async fn handle(&self, invocation: ToolInvocation) -> Result<Self::Output, FunctionCallError> {
34	        let ToolInvocation {
35	            session,
36	            turn,
37	            payload,
38	            ..
39	        } = invocation;
40	
41	        let arguments = match payload {
42	            ToolPayload::Function { arguments } => arguments,
43	            _ => {
44	                return Err(FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(
45	                    "update_goal handler received unsupported payload".to_string(),
46	                ));
47	            }
48	        };
49	
50	        let args: UpdateGoalArgs = parse_arguments(&arguments)?;
51	        if args.status != ThreadGoalStatus::Complete {
52	            return Err(FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(
53	                "update_goal can only mark the existing goal complete; pause, resume, and budget-limited status changes are controlled by the user or system"
54	                    .to_string(),
55	            ));
56	        }
57	        session
58	            .goal_runtime_apply(GoalRuntimeEvent::ToolCompletedGoal {
59	                turn_context: turn.as_ref(),
60	            })
61	            .await
62	            .map_err(|err| FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(format_goal_error(err)))?;
63	        let goal = session
64	            .set_thread_goal(
65	                turn.as_ref(),
66	                SetGoalRequest {
67	                    objective: None,
68	                    status: Some(ThreadGoalStatus::Complete),
69	                    token_budget: None,
70	                },
71	            )
72	            .await
73	            .map_err(|err| FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(format_goal_error(err)))?;
74	        goal_response(Some(goal), CompletionBudgetReport::Include)
75	    }
76	}

109	pub fn validate_acceptance_marker(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<AcceptanceMarker> {
110	    // AS-BUILT §8/§17: completion is accepted only from an external marker
111	    // written by a binary runner and bound to this run_id.
112	    let path = marker_path(state);
113	    let raw = std::fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
114	    let marker: AcceptanceMarker = serde_json::from_slice(&raw).with_json_path(&path)?;
115	    if marker.schema_version != 1 {
116	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
117	            "unsupported acceptance marker schema {}",
118	            marker.schema_version
119	        )));
120	    }
121	    if marker.run_id != state.run_id {
122	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
123	            "acceptance marker run_id {} does not match {}",
124	            marker.run_id, state.run_id
125	        )));
126	    }
127	    if marker.status != "pass" || marker.produced_by != "dr-gate" {
128	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
129	            "acceptance marker was not produced by dr-gate with pass status".to_string(),
130	        ));
131	    }
132	    let expected = marker_signature(&state.run_root, &marker)?;
133	    if marker.signature != expected {
134	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
135	            "acceptance marker signature is invalid; forged self-attestation refused".to_string(),
136	        ));
137	    }
138	    Ok(marker)
139	}

169	    let proofs = run_root.join("proofs");
170	    std::fs::create_dir_all(&proofs).with_path(&proofs)?;
171	    let mut marker = AcceptanceMarker {
172	        schema_version: 1,
173	        run_id,
174	        status: "pass".to_string(),
175	        produced_by: "dr-gate".to_string(),
176	        checked_at: Utc::now(),
177	        working_dir,
178	        signature: String::new(),
179	        check_count: checks.len(),
180	        checks,
181	    };
182	    marker.signature = marker_signature(run_root, &marker)?;
183	    std::fs::write(
184	        proofs.join(ACCEPTANCE_MARKER),
185	        serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&marker).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
186	            path: proofs.join(ACCEPTANCE_MARKER),
187	            source,
188	        })?,
189	    )
190	    .with_path(proofs.join(ACCEPTANCE_MARKER))?;
191	    Ok(marker)
192	}
193	
194	pub fn evaluate_acceptance(
195	    run_root: &Path,
196	    working_dir: &Path,
197	) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
198	    let results = evaluate_acceptance_checks(run_root, working_dir)?;
199	    if let Some(failed) = results
200	        .iter()
201	        .find(|result| result.must_pass && !result.passed)
202	    {
203	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
204	            "acceptance check failed: {}",
205	            failed.detail
206	        )));
207	    }
208	    Ok(results)
209	}
210	
211	pub fn evaluate_acceptance_checks(
212	    run_root: &Path,
213	    working_dir: &Path,
214	) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
215	    let spec_path = acceptance_spec_path_for_run_root(run_root);
216	    if !spec_path.exists() {
217	        return evaluate_default_acceptance(working_dir);
218	    }
219	    let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(&spec_path).with_path(&spec_path)?;
220	    let checks = parse_acceptance_checks(&raw)?;
221	    let mut results = Vec::new();
222	    for check in checks {
223	        let result = evaluate_check(working_dir, check)?;
224	        results.push(result);
225	    }
226	    Ok(results)
227	}
228	
229	fn evaluate_default_acceptance(working_dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheckResult>> {
230	    if working_dir.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
231	        let started = Instant::now();
232	        let output = Command::new("cargo")
233	            .arg("test")
234	            .current_dir(working_dir)
235	            .output()
236	            .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
237	                path: working_dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
238	                source,
239	            })?;
240	        return Ok(vec![AcceptanceCheckResult {
241	            kind: "cargo_test".to_string(),
242	            passed: output.status.success(),
243	            must_pass: true,
244	            detail: format!("cargo test exited with {}", output.status),
245	            command: Some("cargo test".to_string()),
246	            cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
247	            duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
248	            stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
249	            stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
250	        }]);
251	    }
252	    if !working_dir.is_dir() {
253	        return Ok(vec![AcceptanceCheckResult {
254	            kind: "working_dir".to_string(),
255	            passed: false,
256	            must_pass: true,
257	            detail: format!("working directory missing: {}", working_dir.display()),
258	            command: None,
259	            cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
260	            duration_ms: None,
261	            stdout: None,
262	            stderr: None,
263	        }]);
264	    }
265	    Ok(vec![AcceptanceCheckResult {
266	        kind: "working_dir".to_string(),
267	        passed: true,
268	        must_pass: true,
269	        detail: "working directory exists".to_string(),
270	        command: None,
271	        cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
272	        duration_ms: None,
273	        stdout: None,
274	        stderr: None,
275	    }])
276	}
277	
278	fn evaluate_check(working_dir: &Path, check: AcceptanceCheck) -> Result<AcceptanceCheckResult> {
279	    match check {
280	        AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest { args, must_pass } => {
281	            let started = Instant::now();
282	            let output = Command::new("cargo")
283	                .arg("test")
284	                .args(&args)
285	                .current_dir(working_dir)
286	                .output()
287	                .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
288	                    path: working_dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
289	                    source,
290	                })?;
291	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
292	                kind: "cargo_test".to_string(),
293	                passed: output.status.success(),
294	                must_pass,
295	                detail: format!("cargo test exited with {}", output.status),
296	                command: Some(format_command("cargo test", &args)),
297	                cwd: Some(working_dir.to_path_buf()),
298	                duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
299	                stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
300	                stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
301	            })
302	        }
303	        AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { path, must_pass } => {
304	            let path = render_template(working_dir, &path);
305	            let exists = path.exists();
306	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
307	                kind: "file_exists".to_string(),
308	                passed: exists,
309	                must_pass,
310	                detail: if exists {
311	                    format!("{} exists", path.display())
312	                } else {
313	                    format!("{} is missing", path.display())
314	                },
315	                command: None,
316	                cwd: None,
317	                duration_ms: None,
318	                stdout: None,
319	                stderr: None,
320	            })
321	        }
322	        AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch {
323	            path,
324	            pattern,
325	            must_pass,
326	        } => {
327	            let path = render_template(working_dir, &path);
328	            let body = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
329	            let matched = regex::Regex::new(&pattern)
330	                .map(|regex| regex.is_match(&body))
331	                .unwrap_or_else(|_| body.contains(&pattern));
332	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
333	                kind: "content_match".to_string(),
334	                passed: matched,
335	                must_pass,
336	                detail: if matched {
337	                    format!("{} matches {:?}", path.display(), pattern)
338	                } else {
339	                    format!("{} does not match {:?}", path.display(), pattern)
340	                },
341	                command: None,
342	                cwd: None,
343	                duration_ms: None,
344	                stdout: None,
345	                stderr: None,
346	            })
347	        }
348	        AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { cwd, must_pass } => {
349	            let cwd = render_template(working_dir, &cwd);
350	            let started = Instant::now();
351	            let output = Command::new("cargo")
352	                .arg("build")
353	                .current_dir(&cwd)
354	                .output()
355	                .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
356	                    path: cwd.join("Cargo.toml"),
357	                    source,
358	                })?;
359	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
360	                kind: "build_success".to_string(),
361	                passed: output.status.success(),
362	                must_pass,
363	                detail: format!(
364	                    "cargo build in {} exited with {}",
365	                    cwd.display(),
366	                    output.status
367	                ),
368	                command: Some("cargo build".to_string()),
369	                cwd: Some(cwd),
370	                duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
371	                stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
372	                stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
373	            })
374	        }
375	        AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
376	            command,
377	            cwd,
378	            must_pass,
379	        } => {
380	            let cwd = cwd
381	                .map(|cwd| render_template(working_dir, &cwd))
382	                .unwrap_or_else(|| working_dir.to_path_buf());
383	            let started = Instant::now();
384	            let output = Command::new("sh")
385	                .arg("-lc")
386	                .arg(&command)
387	                .current_dir(&cwd)
388	                .output()
389	                .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
390	                    path: cwd.clone(),
391	                    source,
392	                })?;
393	            Ok(AcceptanceCheckResult {
394	                kind: "shell".to_string(),
395	                passed: output.status.success(),
396	                must_pass,
397	                detail: format!(
398	                    "shell {:?} in {} exited with {}",
399	                    command,
400	                    cwd.display(),
401	                    output.status
402	                ),
403	                command: Some(command),
404	                cwd: Some(cwd),
405	                duration_ms: Some(duration_ms(started)),
406	                stdout: clipped_stdout(&output),
407	                stderr: clipped_stderr(&output),
408	            })
409	        }
410	    }
411	}
412	
413	fn duration_ms(started: Instant) -> u64 {
414	    started.elapsed().as_millis().min(u128::from(u64::MAX)) as u64
415	}
416	
417	fn clipped_stdout(output: &Output) -> Option<String> {
418	    clipped_output(&output.stdout)
419	}
420	
421	fn clipped_stderr(output: &Output) -> Option<String> {
422	    clipped_output(&output.stderr)
423	}
424	
425	fn clipped_output(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
426	    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).trim().to_string();
427	    if text.is_empty() {
428	        None
429	    } else {
430	        Some(clip_text(&text, 4096))
431	    }
432	}
433	
434	fn clip_text(text: &str, limit: usize) -> String {
435	    if text.len() <= limit {
436	        return text.to_string();
437	    }
438	    let mut clipped = text
439	        .char_indices()
440	        .take_while(|(idx, _)| *idx < limit)
441	        .map(|(_, ch)| ch)
442	        .collect::<String>();
443	    clipped.push_str("\n... output truncated ...");
444	    clipped
445	}
446	
447	fn format_command(base: &str, args: &[String]) -> String {
448	    if args.is_empty() {
449	        base.to_string()
450	    } else {
451	        format!("{base} {}", args.join(" "))
452	    }
453	}
454	
455	fn parse_acceptance_checks(raw: &str) -> Result<Vec<AcceptanceCheck>> {
456	    let root: YamlValue = serde_yaml::from_str(raw).map_err(|source| {
457	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("invalid acceptance.yaml: {source}"))
458	    })?;
459	    let mut checks = Vec::new();
460	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "checks")) {
461	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item.clone(), None)?);
462	    }
463	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "required")) {
464	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item.clone(), Some(true))?);
465	    }
466	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "optional")) {
467	        checks.push(parse_check_value(item.clone(), Some(false))?);
468	    }
469	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "tests")) {
470	        checks.push(parse_shell_check(item.clone(), true)?);
471	    }
472	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "file-exists")) {
473	        checks.push(parse_file_exists_check(item.clone(), true)?);
474	    }
475	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "content-match")) {
476	        checks.push(parse_content_match_check(item.clone(), true)?);
477	    }
478	    for item in yaml_seq(yaml_get(&root, "build-success")) {
479	        checks.push(parse_build_success_check(item.clone(), true)?);
480	    }
481	    Ok(checks)
482	}
483	
484	fn parse_check_value(value: YamlValue, force_must_pass: Option<bool>) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
485	    if let Ok(mut check) = serde_yaml::from_value::<AcceptanceCheck>(value.clone()) {
486	        if let Some(must_pass) = force_must_pass {
487	            check.set_must_pass(must_pass);
488	        }
489	        return Ok(check);
490	    }
491	    if let Some(command) = yaml_string(&value) {
492	        return Ok(AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
493	            command,
494	            cwd: None,
495	            must_pass: force_must_pass.unwrap_or(true),
496	        });
497	    }
498	    let Some((kind, body)) = single_key_mapping(&value) else {
499	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
500	            "invalid acceptance check: {:?}",
501	            value
502	        )));
503	    };
504	    let must_pass = force_must_pass.unwrap_or(true);
505	    match kind.as_str() {
506	        "file-exists" | "file_exists" => parse_file_exists_check(body.clone(), must_pass),
507	        "content-match" | "content_match" => parse_content_match_check(body.clone(), must_pass),
508	        "build-success" | "build_success" => parse_build_success_check(body.clone(), must_pass),
509	        "shell" | "test" => parse_shell_check(body.clone(), must_pass),
510	        "cargo-test" | "cargo_test" => Ok(AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest {
511	            args: yaml_string(body).map(|arg| vec![arg]).unwrap_or_default(),
512	            must_pass,
513	        }),
514	        other => Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
515	            "unknown acceptance check kind {other}"
516	        ))),
517	    }
518	}
519	
520	fn parse_file_exists_check(value: YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
521	    let path = yaml_string(&value)
522	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(&value, "path").and_then(yaml_string))
523	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("file-exists requires path".to_string()))?;
524	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { path, must_pass })
525	}
526	
527	fn parse_content_match_check(value: YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
528	    let path = yaml_get(&value, "path")
529	        .and_then(yaml_string)
530	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("content-match requires path".to_string()))?;
531	    let pattern = yaml_get(&value, "pattern")
532	        .and_then(yaml_string)
533	        .ok_or_else(|| {
534	            DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("content-match requires pattern".to_string())
535	        })?;
536	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch {
537	        path,
538	        pattern,
539	        must_pass,
540	    })
541	}
542	
543	fn parse_build_success_check(value: YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
544	    let cwd = yaml_string(&value)
545	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(&value, "cwd").and_then(yaml_string))
546	        .unwrap_or_else(|| "{working_dir}".to_string());
547	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { cwd, must_pass })
548	}
549	
550	fn parse_shell_check(value: YamlValue, must_pass: bool) -> Result<AcceptanceCheck> {
551	    let command = yaml_string(&value)
552	        .or_else(|| yaml_get(&value, "command").and_then(yaml_string))
553	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::InvalidInput("shell check requires command".to_string()))?;
554	    let cwd = yaml_get(&value, "cwd").and_then(yaml_string);
555	    Ok(AcceptanceCheck::Shell {
556	        command,
557	        cwd,
558	        must_pass,
559	    })
560	}
561	
562	fn yaml_get<'a>(value: &'a YamlValue, key: &str) -> Option<&'a YamlValue> {
563	    value.as_mapping()?.get(YamlValue::String(key.to_string()))
564	}
565	
566	fn yaml_seq(value: Option<&YamlValue>) -> Vec<&YamlValue> {
567	    match value {
568	        Some(YamlValue::Sequence(values)) => values.iter().collect(),
569	        Some(value) => vec![value],
570	        None => Vec::new(),
571	    }
572	}
573	
574	fn yaml_string(value: &YamlValue) -> Option<String> {
575	    value.as_str().map(ToString::to_string)
576	}
577	
578	fn single_key_mapping(value: &YamlValue) -> Option<(String, &YamlValue)> {
579	    let mapping = value.as_mapping()?;
580	    if mapping.len() != 1 {
581	        return None;
582	    }
583	    let (key, value) = mapping.iter().next()?;
584	    Some((key.as_str()?.to_string(), value))
585	}
586	
587	impl AcceptanceCheck {
588	    fn set_must_pass(&mut self, value: bool) {
589	        match self {
590	            AcceptanceCheck::CargoTest { must_pass, .. }
591	            | AcceptanceCheck::FileExists { must_pass, .. }
592	            | AcceptanceCheck::ContentMatch { must_pass, .. }
593	            | AcceptanceCheck::BuildSuccess { must_pass, .. }
594	            | AcceptanceCheck::Shell { must_pass, .. } => *must_pass = value,
595	        }
596	    }
597	}
598	
599	fn render_template(working_dir: &Path, value: &str) -> PathBuf {
600	    PathBuf::from(value.replace("{working_dir}", &working_dir.to_string_lossy()))
601	}
602	
603	fn marker_signature(run_root: &Path, marker: &AcceptanceMarker) -> Result<String> {
604	    let nonce_path = gate_nonce_path_for_run_root(run_root);
605	    let nonce = std::fs::read_to_string(&nonce_path).with_path(&nonce_path)?;
606	    let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();
607	    nonce.trim().hash(&mut hasher);
608	    marker.schema_version.hash(&mut hasher);
609	    marker.run_id.hash(&mut hasher);
610	    marker.status.hash(&mut hasher);
611	    marker.produced_by.hash(&mut hasher);
612	    marker.checked_at.to_rfc3339().hash(&mut hasher);
613	    marker.working_dir.hash(&mut hasher);
614	    marker.check_count.hash(&mut hasher);
615	    for check in &marker.checks {
616	        check.hash(&mut hasher);
617	    }
618	    Ok(format!("{:016x}", hasher.finish()))
619	}
620	
621	fn default_must_pass() -> bool {
622	    true
623	}

35	- For each item, determine whether the evidence proves completion, contradicts completion, shows incomplete work, is too weak or indirect to verify completion, or is missing.
36	- Match the verification scope to the requirement's scope; do not use a narrow check to support a broad claim.
37	- Treat tests, manifests, verifiers, green checks, and search results as evidence only after confirming they cover the relevant requirement.

Only mark the goal achieved when current evidence proves every requirement has been satisfied and no required work remains. If the evidence is incomplete, weak, indirect, merely consistent with completion, or leaves any requirement missing, incomplete, or unverified, keep working instead of marking the goal complete. 1	# deadreckon Alpha Design
2	
3	## Product
4	
5	`deadreckon` is a Rust 2024 CLI harness for unattended long-running coding tasks. The default user flow is `deadreckon run <goal>`: create durable run state, select a BYOK provider route, execute turns in a disposable sandbox, write spend/provenance/traces/snapshots after every turn, and make the run attachable, resumable, killable, inspectable, and undoable.
6	
7	The alpha implementation is intentionally local-first. Runtime state defaults to `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`, and tests or explicit smoke runs can override that with `DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke` so this build process does not write outside the allowed implementation tree.
8	
9	## Reference Patterns
10	
11	- AS-BUILT §3: two-layer split. Rust owns state, locks, sandboxes, provider routing, and gates. Markdown skills under `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/` own agent-facing instructions.
12	- AS-BUILT §4: `state.json` per run, status enum, gap-numbered phase IDs, and `current/<task>.json` run pointers.
13	- AS-BUILT §6: JSON lock records with PID liveness and heartbeat stale reclaim.
14	- AS-BUILT §7-8: atomic promotion/gate markers are written by binary-owned verification, not by model prose.
15	- AS-BUILT §9: per-turn snapshots make bounded rollback possible.
16	- Claude Code mining:
17	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/tools/BashTool/bashPermissions.ts` and `shouldUseSandbox.ts` inform command side-effect boundaries and sandbox warning posture.
18	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/tools/shared/spawnMultiAgent.ts` informs inherited run context for future sub-agent work; alpha records scope and session lineage but leaves explicit forks to V1.
19	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/upstreamproxy/upstreamproxy.ts` informs fail-open provider/proxy setup and child-process environment merging.
20	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/ink/renderer.ts` informs ratatui attach rendering: bounded frames, no uncontrolled terminal state.
21	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/docs/prompts/` informs the Markdown skill shape in `skills/default-coding/SKILL.md`.
22	
23	## Workspace
24	
25	Source lives under `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`:
26	
27	- `crates/deadreckon-core`: run paths, phase machine, JSON state, codebase mode records, locks, heartbeats, snapshots, provenance, spend, traces, gates, imports, chains, and run docs primitives.
28	- `crates/deadreckon-runtime`: provider turn loop, sandboxed tool dispatch, cancellation checks, docs polish orchestration, `dr-gate` invocation, and promotion orchestration.
29	- `crates/deadreckon-providers`: BYOK config at `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`, provider trait, Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible, `cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`, and explicit `--smoke` scripted adapters, fallback routing, spend estimates.
30	- `crates/deadreckon-sandbox`: `sandbox-exec`, `bwrap`, `docker`, and `none` backends using `tokio::process::Command`; default `auto`.
31	- `crates/deadreckon`: clap parser, command handlers, ratatui attach UI, init/setup, config/settings, run, status/next, list/runs, doc/docs, attach/watch, kill/stop, resume/continue, undo/restore, show/inspect, import, materialize/export, finish/done, apply/keep, abandon/discard, cleanup/prune, extend/follow-up, library/artifacts, chain, and doctor/check.
32	- `skills/default-coding/SKILL.md`: Markdown skill loaded at runtime.
33	- `tests/`: workspace integration tests.
34	
35	## Top-10 Need Mapping
36	
37	1. Live Context & Spend Meter: `spend.jsonl` in `deadreckon-core`, spend summaries in `deadreckon attach`.
38	2. Multi-Agent Worktree Coordination: scope hashing, run pointers, and locks in `deadreckon-core`.
39	3. Infinite Undo For Agent Edits: per-turn `snapshots/turn-<N>/` plus `deadreckon undo`.
40	4. Prompt-To-Code Provenance Audit Trail: `provenance.jsonl` and `deadreckon show`.
41	5. Cross-Tool State Sharing: read-only import from `/Users/gdc/.claude/projects/`, `/Users/gdc/.codex/sessions/`, `/Users/gdc/.cursor/chats/`.
42	6. Agent Observability: `traces.jsonl` with LLM/tool/sandbox events and latencies.
43	7. Disposable Sandboxes: platform-native sandbox backends, Docker opt-in, `none` warning.
44	8. Billing Guardrails: `--max-spend <USD>` pauses runs when durable spend reaches cap.
45	9. Provider Routing / BYOK: adapters, CLI sub-agents, `deadreckon init`, `deadreckon config get/set`, and fallback chain configured from TOML.
46	10. Workspace Inventory & Run Queue: project-scoped `list`, `status`/`next`, `latest` run aliases, `attach`, `kill`, `resume`, `cleanup`, and state scan commands.
47	
48	## Execution Model
49	
50	The primary path is provider-driven: `deadreckon run <goal>` resolves the
51	codebase mode, previews the plan, creates state, and hands execution to
52	`deadreckon-runtime`. The runtime calls `ProviderRouter::complete`, parses model
53	actions, executes tool calls in the configured sandbox, feeds results into
54	history, writes docs, invokes `dr-gate`, and promotes successful runs. It
55	repeats until a provider returns `done`, a spend cap pauses the run, or the run
56	is killed. HTTP providers use user-supplied keys or env vars; CLI providers use
57	local subscription CLIs and run through the deadreckon sandbox wrapper.
58	
59	In a git repo, the default codebase mode is `worktree`: deadreckon creates
60	`~/.deadreckon/worktrees/<scope>-<run-id>` on a `dr/...` branch, runs the agent
61	there, and leaves the user's checkout untouched until `deadreckon apply`. Outside
62	git, interactive users can initialize git, copy the directory, or cancel.
63	Non-interactive users must pass `--fresh`, `--from`, or initialize git first.
64	The former empty working directory path remains available as `--fresh`.
65	
66	For keyless local verification only, `deadreckon run --smoke <goal>` selects the `smoke` provider explicitly. That scripted provider still goes through the same turn loop, sandbox dispatch, snapshots, spend records, traces, provenance, and external `dr-gate` acceptance marker; it is not the default run path.
67	
68	The default skill is Markdown and external to the binary. The binary loads it and records the skill name/path in state; it does not parse or mutate skill internals.
69	
70	## CLI Lifecycle
71	
72	Completed artifacts are promoted into `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/library/<scope>/<run-id>/`.
73	Worktree runs keep their `dr/...` branch available for review and finish with
74	`deadreckon finish <run-id>`, `deadreckon apply <run-id>`, or
75	`deadreckon abandon <run-id>`. `done` aliases `finish`, `keep` aliases `apply`,
76	and `discard` aliases `abandon`. `apply` supports squash, merge, and
77	cherry-pick strategies; `abandon` removes the worktree and, unless
78	`--keep-branch` is used, the temporary branch.
79	
80	Copy and fresh runs use `deadreckon materialize <run-id> --dest <path>` or the
81	`deadreckon export <run-id> --dest <path>` alias to copy the library artifact to
82	a user-owned path. `deadreckon finish <run-id> --dest <path>` routes to the same
83	export behavior for copy/fresh runs. These commands write
84	`.deadreckon/parent.json` and record the reverse `.materialized-to` marker in
85	the library. `deadreckon extend
86	<run-id> "follow-up goal"` preserves the parent's mode semantics: worktree
87	parents create a child `dr/...` branch off the parent branch, copy/fresh parents
88	seed a new working tree from the parent library, and in-place parents refuse with
89	a direct `run --in-place` hint. Extended runs store parent lineage in
90	`working/.deadreckon/parent.json` and start the normal turn loop with reset
91	resource caps.
92	
93	For normal operation, run ids accept unique prefixes and `latest` / `last`
94	resolve to the most recent run in the current project scope. `deadreckon list`
95	defaults to that current scope, `deadreckon list --all` shows global history, and
96	running `deadreckon` without a subcommand is equivalent to `deadreckon status`.
97	`deadreckon cleanup` / `deadreckon prune` remove abandoned, stale, or explicitly
98	selected completed worktree runs while leaving promoted library artifacts in
99	place.
100	
101	Lineage and codebase mode metadata intentionally stay outside `PipelineState`;
102	show/list/hints derive them from marker files and `working/.deadreckon/codebase.json`
103	so the state schema remains stable.
104	
105	Self-documenting run artifacts also live outside `PipelineState`. Each run
106	starts `working/.deadreckon/docs/`, appends deterministic per-turn records, and
107	attempts one `run-narrator` polish pass before promotion unless `--no-docs` is
108	set. Public copies land under `docs/` in the promoted artifact, and `apply`
109	builds its default commit body from the narrative and decisions docs.
110	
111	## Decisions And Conflicts
112	
113	- Runtime writes during verification: the rider prescribes `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`, while the build instruction forbids edits outside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/` and `/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/goals/`. The binary defaults to `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`, but all repository verification uses `DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke`.
114	- Sub-agent forking: the architecture requires the pattern, but the V1 list explicitly moves `deadreckon fork` to V1. Alpha records scope/session lineage and keeps the subprocess skill boundary; explicit multi-agent forks are documented in `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
115	- Sandbox fallback: on macOS `auto` selects `sandbox-exec` if available. If not available, or on Linux without `bwrap`, `doctor` reports the missing binary and `run` falls back to `none` with a warning, matching the rider.
116	- Live Tier C CLI verification: `codex` was run with `exec --ephemeral --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` inside deadreckon's outer `sandbox-exec` wrapper. Run `59c57e4565704135a9982789d0754803` produced `working/notes.md`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, snapshots, and a validated `dr-gate` marker without raw API keys.
117	- First-run UX: `deadreckon init` writes `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`, `deadreckon config get/set` performs non-interactive edits, `doctor` prints actionable check/fix lines, and `run` enforces the `$50` confirmation guard for scripts.
118	- Codebase modes: the architecture keeps mode metadata in
119	  `working/.deadreckon/codebase.json` rather than extending `PipelineState`.
120	  This preserves existing runstate readers while allowing worktree, copy,
121	  in-place, and fresh flows to evolve independently.
122	- Crate boundary: `deadreckon-core` is adapter-free and owns durable schemas and
123	  primitives. `deadreckon-runtime` owns the dependencies on providers and
124	  sandboxes, so core tests and downstream readers can reason about state without
125	  pulling in HTTP, subprocess, or platform sandbox orchestration.
126

1	# deadreckon — Build Rider (V0)
2	
3	This rider holds the prescriptive constraints for the goal at
4	`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-05-10-1400-deadreckon-build-goal.md`.
5	Read it before writing code. Sections marked "do not violate" are hard constraints.
6	
7	**All paths in this document are absolute. Generated code, config, docs, and
8	verification scripts must use absolute paths or paths anchored to a single
9	known root (`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/` for source, `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`
10	for runtime state). No bare relative paths in user-visible artifacts.**
11	
12	## Product framing (decided — do not redesign)
13	
14	- **What it is.** A Rust CLI agent harness whose default flow is **unattended long-running coding tasks**. The user types one goal, hits enter, and the harness drives the task across hours of model time — sandboxed, crash-resumable, spend-capped, with full provenance.
15	- **What it isn't.** Not an editor, not a chat app, not an MCP framework, not a CI runner, not a kitchen-sink agent IDE.
16	- **Target user.** Solo developers and ≤ 10-person teams currently paying $200+/month per seat across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, opencode, and still doing manual bookkeeping for spend, undo, and multi-agent coordination.
17	- **BYOK posture.** Multi-provider from day one, opencode-style. The user supplies keys; the harness never bills usage. V0 providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, plus an OpenAI-compatible shim (OpenRouter, llama.cpp, etc.).
18	- **Name.** **deadreckon.** Dead reckoning is navigation by integrating known motion from a fixed starting point — no GPS, no external check. The harness drives long-running agent work the same way: durable state at every turn, no live human in the loop, no live model attestation, reconstructable position after any crash.
19	
20	## Architecture (decided — do not redesign)
21	
22	Adopt these patterns from `/Users/gdc/Downloads/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md`. Each
23	adoption cites the AS-BUILT section in a code comment near the implementation.
24	
25	- **Two-layer split.** Rust binary owns state, locks, sandboxes, gates, atomic file ops, sub-agent management. Agent-facing skill layer (markdown skills loaded at runtime) owns judgment, prose, orchestration. The skill is invoked as a sub-process; the binary never reaches into skill internals. (AS-BUILT §3)
26	- **Phase machine with on-disk state.** `state.json` per run, status enum (`pending|planned|executing|completed|failed`), gap-numbered phase IDs. (AS-BUILT §4)
27	- **Run pointer + run scoping.** `current/<task>.json` points at the active run per task; `runs/<run-id>/` carries durable state. Scope hash from git root or env var lets parallel worktrees coexist. (AS-BUILT §4)
28	- **Locks with heartbeats + PID liveness.** Process-held locks survive crash detection via PID-zero kill probe; stale locks reclaimable after timeout. (AS-BUILT §6)
29	- **Atomic promotion.** Work happens in `working/`; promoted atomically to `library/` only after a gate marker is written. (AS-BUILT §7)
30	- **Anti-self-attestation gates.** Acceptance markers (test pass, sandbox green, spend within cap) can only be written by an external runner and are validated by the binary against the run identity. The agent cannot self-mark a gate. (AS-BUILT §8, §17)
31	- **Sub-agent forking with context isolation.** Research-heavy or diagnostic-heavy sub-tasks run in forked subprocess agents; they return structured summaries to the parent. (AS-BUILT §10)
32	- **Bounded fix loops with rollback.** Every code mutation is backed up, build-checked, regression-checked, and rolled back on failure within a retry budget. (AS-BUILT §9)
33	
34	## Patterns to mine from Claude Code source (`/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/`)
35	
36	The Claude Code source is a working reference for the user-facing primitives
37	this harness needs. Read these subtrees before implementing the relevant
38	crate; cite the file in a code comment when adopting a pattern.
39	
40	- **Tool-use loop and turn structure** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/assistant/`. How the assistant runs a turn, schedules tool calls, handles streaming, and unwinds on errors. Inform `deadreckon-core`'s run loop.
41	- **Tool implementations and permission model** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/tools/`. Per-tool permission gates, parameter schemas, side-effect boundaries, the analogue of `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Inform `deadreckon-core` tool dispatch, the platform-sandbox profile (filesystem/network/env scope), and the `--sandbox none` warning.
42	- **Task / coordinator orchestration** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/tasks/`, `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/coordinator/`. Multi-task supervision, sub-agent forking patterns. Inform `deadreckon`'s `run/attach/kill/resume`.
43	- **Upstream proxy / provider abstraction** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/upstreamproxy/`. How Claude Code shapes requests, handles streaming, retries, and tool-result feedback. Inform `deadreckon-providers`.
44	- **TUI patterns** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/ink/`. React-Ink reference for a streaming, attachable terminal UI; port idioms to `ratatui` rather than copying React.
45	- **Prompts and skill structure** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/docs/prompts/`. Existing system prompt shapes, skill loading conventions. Inform `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/default-coding/SKILL.md`.
46	
47	**Rust adaptations (use these crates, no alternatives in V0):**
48	
49	- `tokio` — async runtime.
50	- `serde` + `serde_json` — state serialization.
51	- `nix` (Unix) + `fs2` — advisory file locking + PID liveness via `kill(pid, 0)`.
52	- `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` — structured logs / observability.
53	- `clap` derive — CLI parsing.
54	- `ratatui` + `crossterm` — TUI.
55	- `reqwest` — HTTP client for provider calls.
56	- `which` — locate `sandbox-exec` / `bwrap` / `docker` binaries at preflight time. Sandbox backends shell out via `tokio::process::Command`; no Docker SDK dep.
57	- Cargo workspace: separate crates for `deadreckon-core`, `deadreckon-providers`, `deadreckon-sandbox`, `deadreckon` (bin).
58	
59	## Must-have unmet needs (V0 scope)
60	
61	Each implementation slice maps to ≥ 1 of these. Comment in the source where
62	each is implemented (e.g., `// REPORT.md: Live Context & Spend Meter`).
63	
64	1. **Live Context & Spend Meter** — `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/runstate/<scope>/runs/<id>/spend.jsonl` (durable per-turn telemetry); surfaces in TUI.
65	2. **Multi-Agent Worktree Coordination** — scopes + lock primitives let N agents run in parallel without conflict.
66	3. **Infinite Undo for Agent Edits** — `snapshots/turn-<N>/` per run; `deadreckon undo` restores to any prior turn.
67	4. **Prompt-to-Code Provenance Audit Trail** — `provenance.jsonl` per run; every file change carries `{ prompt_id, model, tool_call_id, timestamp, session_id, files: [...] }`.
68	5. **Cross-Tool State Sharing (read-only import)** — `deadreckon import claude-code|codex|cursor` reads `/Users/gdc/.claude/projects/`, `/Users/gdc/.codex/sessions/`, `/Users/gdc/.cursor/chats/`. No live bridging in V0.
69	6. **Agent Observability** — `traces.jsonl` per run (LLM calls, tool calls, retries, latency); exportable.
70	7. **Disposable Sandboxes** — platform-native per run by default (`sandbox-exec` on macOS, `bubblewrap` on Linux); `--sandbox auto|sandbox-exec|bwrap|docker|none` flag, default `auto`.
71	8. **Billing Guardrails** — `--max-spend <USD>` flag; mid-run pause when cap is hit; resume requires explicit user OK.
72	9. **Provider Routing / BYOK** — multi-provider with fallback chain configured in `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`.
73	10. **Workspace Inventory & Run Queue** — `deadreckon list/attach/kill/resume` over `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/runstate/`.
74	
75	## V0 prescribed decisions (do not deliberate)
76	
77	These resolve the open options that would otherwise belong in a design doc.
78	
79	- **Sandbox primary.** Platform-native: `sandbox-exec` (Seatbelt) on macOS, `bubblewrap` (`bwrap`) on Linux. Flag `--sandbox auto|sandbox-exec|bwrap|docker|none`; default `auto` (auto-selects the platform-native backend). Docker is `--sandbox docker` opt-in for users who want it. Lima / Firecracker / E2B / Landlock are V1 candidates. No `bollard` dep — backends shell out via `tokio::process::Command`.
80	- **Plugin / skill language.** Markdown skills, Claude-Code-style. Loaded at runtime from `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/`. WASM plugins are V1.
81	- **State store.** Plain JSON files, atomically written via temp+rename. SQLite cache is V1.
82	- **TUI framework.** `ratatui` + `crossterm`.
83	- **Provider abstraction.** Custom `Provider` trait per provider; one OpenAI-compatible shim that handles any compliant endpoint (lets users plug in OpenRouter, llama.cpp).
84	
85	## Source tree layout (`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`)
86	
87	```
88	/Users/gdc/deadreckon/
89	├── Cargo.toml                          # workspace
90	├── DESIGN.md                           # phase-0 artifact
91	├── README.md                           # how to install + run
92	├── demo.cast                           # asciinema of end-to-end smoke
93	├── crates/
94	│   ├── deadreckon-core/                # state, locks, phase engine, snapshots
95	│   ├── deadreckon-providers/           # BYOK router (Anthropic, OpenAI, openai-compat)
96	│   ├── deadreckon-sandbox/             # backends: sandbox-exec / bwrap / docker / none
97	│   └── deadreckon/                     # binary (clap CLI + TUI)
98	├── skills/                             # markdown skills loaded at runtime
99	│   └── default-coding/SKILL.md
100	└── tests/                              # workspace integration tests
101	```
102	
103	## Runtime state layout (`/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`)
104	
105	```
106	/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/
107	├── config.toml                         # BYOK keys, default provider, defaults
108	├── runstate/
109	│   └── <scope>/
110	│       ├── current/<task>.json         # active run pointer per task
111	│       └── runs/<run-id>/
112	│           ├── state.json              # PipelineState
113	│           ├── snapshots/turn-<N>/     # per-turn file snapshots
114	│           ├── provenance.jsonl        # one line per file change
115	│           ├── spend.jsonl             # one line per turn cost
116	│           ├── traces.jsonl            # LLM + tool call traces
117	│           └── working/                # in-progress task workdir
118	├── locks/<task>.lock                   # active build locks
119	└── library/<scope>/<run-id>/           # archived completed runs
120	```
121	
122	## CLI surface (must implement in V0)
123	
124	- `deadreckon run <goal> [--max-spend <USD>] [--sandbox auto|sandbox-exec|bwrap|docker|none] [--provider anthropic|openai|...] [--skill <name>]`
125	- `deadreckon list [--scope <scope>]` — list runs (active + recent).
126	- `deadreckon attach <run-id>` — open the live TUI on an in-flight or completed run.
127	- `deadreckon kill <run-id>` — terminate cleanly, release lock.
128	- `deadreckon resume <run-id>` — re-attach after a crash or pause; respects the phase machine.
129	- `deadreckon undo [--run <run-id>] [--turn <N>]` — restore files to N turns ago.
130	- `deadreckon show <run-id> [--turn <N>]` — print state, files changed, provenance.
131	- `deadreckon import {claude-code|codex|cursor}` — read-only import of histories.
132	- `deadreckon doctor` — preflight: platform sandbox binary reachable (`sandbox-exec` on mac, `bwrap` on Linux), Docker present only if `--sandbox docker` was used, config present, providers credentialed. Output is **actionable**: each missing item names the exact fix command.
133	- `deadreckon init` — first-run wizard. Interactively gathers ≥ 1 provider key (Anthropic / OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible URL + key), sets a default `--max-spend`, writes `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`, runs `doctor`, prints next steps. Re-runnable; merges over existing config.
134	- `deadreckon config get <key>` / `deadreckon config set <key> <value>` — non-interactive config edits. Keys: `providers.anthropic.api_key`, `providers.openai.api_key`, `defaults.max_spend`, `defaults.sandbox`, etc.
135	
136	## User-friendliness (V0 commitments — do not violate)
137	
138	User-friendliness is a V0 requirement, not a V1 polish item. The build agent
139	must budget UX work into every relevant phase. These commitments override
140	engineering-elegance preferences when they conflict.
141	
142	### 1. First-run experience is one command
143	
144	A new user reaches their first successful run in three commands:
145	
146	```zsh
147	deadreckon init                              # interactive: pick provider, paste key, set defaults
148	deadreckon run "hello-world in rust"         # respects defaults from init
149	deadreckon attach <run-id>                   # live TUI
150	```
151	
152	No manual `config.toml` editing required. `init` is the only acceptable
153	first-time path.
154	
155	### 2. Errors include a one-line fix hint
156	
157	Every `DeadreckonError` variant carries a `hint: &'static str` field rendered
158	after the message. A missing API key surfaces as:
159	
160	```
161	error: Anthropic API key not configured
162	  hint: run `deadreckon config set providers.anthropic.api_key <KEY>`
163	        or `deadreckon init` to walk through setup
164	```
165	
166	No bare HTTP status codes, no stack traces in user-facing output. Stack
167	traces go to `tracing` logs only (`--verbose` reveals them).
168	
169	### 3. Sensible spend default with explicit confirmation above
170	
171	- `--max-spend` defaults to `$10` if not specified.
172	- Running without `--max-spend` on a fresh session prints a one-line notice
173	  the first time: `using default --max-spend $10 (override with --max-spend or
174	  in config defaults.max_spend)`.
175	- Setting `--max-spend > $50` requires `--i-know-its-a-lot` or a `y/N`
176	  confirmation prompt (with `--no-confirm` to override in scripts).
177	
178	### 4. `doctor` output is actionable
179	
180	Each line is either `✓ <thing>` or `✗ <thing>` followed by the exact fix.
181	
182	```
183	✓ sandbox-exec found at /usr/bin/sandbox-exec
184	✗ Docker not found
185	    fix: install Docker Desktop (https://docker.com/get-started)
186	         or run with --sandbox sandbox-exec (default on macOS)
187	✓ /Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml present
188	✗ no Anthropic key configured
189	    fix: deadreckon config set providers.anthropic.api_key <KEY>
190	✓ ~250 MB free in /Users/gdc/.deadreckon (heads-up at 50 MB)
191	```
192	
193	### 5. Quickstart in README, top of page
194	
195	`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/README.md` opens with a "Quickstart" section that runs
196	in under two minutes for a user with an Anthropic key. The three-command flow
197	from §1 plus one expected-output block.
198	
199	### 6. TUI visual feedback
200
```
